To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a supervised machine learning model trained to classify eye gaze data from mind wandering and normal computerized reading can be used to predict mind wandering with high accuracy and that these predictions are correlated with self reported mind wandering and predict comprehension better than do self reports.
a supervised machine learning model can be used to objectively detect mind wandering during reading with a level of accuracy that is sufficient to predict text comprehension.
a model based measure of mind wandering, trained on eye gaze during reading, is internally consistent and predicts text comprehension more strongly that does self reporting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and testing objective, eye gaze based measures of mind wandering during text comprehension, which may be used as a tool to study this ubiquitous and important phenomenon.
the development of an objective measure of mind wandering that can be used to study the phenomenon in the context of a computerized reading task.
the development of a new method for studying mind wandering during reading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study show that a model based measure of mind wandering, based on eye tracking, can be developed and that it has the potential to provide a more objective measure than self reports.

this study has demonstrated that it is possible to develop a reliable automated objective measure of mind wandering that can predict text comprehension, but that this measure is still in need of further development and validation.

we have shown that an eye gaze based model of mind wandering can be trained and tested in a new group of participants, and can be used to estimate the level of mind wandering experienced by individual readers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

mind wandering can be objectively measured using eye tracking, which is important for the field of psychology because self reports are subjective and can be biased by the participant's memory of what they were thinking about while reading.
we have developed a new, objective, and automated measure of mind wandering.
mind wandering is not only a subjective experience, but also a behavioral phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to develop a model that predicts mind wandering during reading with sufficient accuracy to warrant its use as a measure in future research.
the eye gaze data can be analyzed to produce an objective measure of mind wandering that is consistent with self reports and can predict text comprehension.
mind wandering during reading can be objectively measured with an eye tracker and a machine learned classifier.
